To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the viral load of H r-HPV types can be used to define a cut-off that improves the specificity of H r- HPV DNA tests for the detection of cervical lesions.

viral load of high-risk HPV types is an excellent predictor for the presence of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) grade 2+ in women with atypical squamos cells of undetermined signifance (ASCUS) or low grade squamos intraepithelial neoplasia (LSIL), and that the use of viral load as predictor for CIN grade 2+ is independent of the type-specific HPV test used.
high viral load of high-risk HPV types is a reliable predictor for the presence of cervical lesions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new diagnostic tools for cervical cancer screening and triage.
the development of new molecular diagnostic methods for the detection and typing of human papillomavirus (HPV).
the detection and identification of HPV DNA and its application in clinical practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HPV viral load is an independent and reliable marker for the presence of cervical lesions.

HPV viral load is a very useful and reliable clinical predictor for the presence of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) and Cervical Cancer (CC) and can be used as a very important tool to help clinicians in making decisions on the management of patients with HPV-related lesions.
HPV DNA testing has a high sensitivity for detecting CIN2+ in women with ASC-US, LSIL, and HSIL cytology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the viral load is a very good predictor for the presence of CIN3+ lesions.
the viral load is a reliable marker to identify the risk of cervical cancer.

we have developed a new method for the detection and quantification of HPV DNA in clinical specimens and we have shown that this method has a higher sensitivity than other methods for the detection of high-risk HPV DNA in clinical samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of quantitative HPV DNA testing may help in reducing the amount of false-positive results detected by the current HPV DNA tests.
high viral load is a reliable predictor for the presence of a high-grade lesion, and that the viral load of the individual HPV type is a better predictor than a composite viral load.
viral loads are more specific than DNA positivity alone in the detection of cervical lesions.
